name: RepoProbe
role: benchmark (dataset + official checklist scorer + Docker-isolated reference harness)
commit_note: Latest commit at audit time ("Pin upstream repositories to their snapshot commits and link the arXiv preprint"). Repo first published 2026-08-05/06 -- very new, no release tags, minimal community track record.
license_data: CC BY 4.0 (original GitHub Discussion text copyright remains with original authors)
environment_strategy: no vendoring of the Docker harness or dataset_loader.py; vendored ONLY prompt_templates_en.py (the scoring prompt template file) with this manifest as provenance. Dataset CSVs and repos_info.json are fetched live from the pinned commit's raw content at load time, never locally re-typed.
judge_model_note: RepoProbe's own released code defaults its judge to gpt-5.2; its paper's own headline number used claude-sonnet-4-5 instead. This evaluation suite deliberately uses neither -- every LLM-judged benchmark in this suite is judged by the SAME centralized GPT-5 snapshot (ant.evaluation_suite.judge.DEFAULT_JUDGE_MODEL, gpt-5-2025-08-07) so that judge-model choice is held constant across every system compared here. This is a disclosed, deliberate fairness choice, not a fidelity gap or a blocker -- see judge.py's own module docstring.
local_modifications: CSV parsing uses Python's stdlib csv module instead of pandas (RepoProbe's own dataset_loader.py dependency) -- same column mapping (taxonomy/difficulty/question/answer/checklist), verified against the official loader's own column_mapping dict.

Scoring prompt template vendored verbatim from prompt_templates_en.py (DIRECT_SCORING_WITH_REPO_TEMPLATE), not paraphrased -- the checklist rubric itself (knowledge_score/9 + clarity_score/1) is unchanged from the official template.

Judge call uses this suite's own centralized GPT-5 judge (src/ant/evaluation_suite/judge.py, OpenAI Responses API) instead of RepoProbe's own judge (whether its code-default gpt-5.2 or its paper's claude-sonnet-4-5) -- an intentional standardization, not a workaround for a missing credential.

repo_info_section's directory_structure is NOT populated via repomix (a Node.js tool, deliberately not vendored to avoid a new non-Python toolchain dependency) -- passed empty instead. This is a disclosed, minor fidelity gap affecting only supplementary prompt context, not the scored checklist itself.

n_scalar_calls=3 (three independent judge calls, mean total score) -- this suite's own uniform internal stabilization policy applied to every LLM-scalar benchmark, not an attempt to match RepoProbe's own main-table protocol (a single call; RepoProbe's own 5-run averaging is a separate RQ2-only stability-analysis experiment).
official_reference_agent_status: NOT executed live in this session -- the paper's own headline system is Claude Code (a separate CLI tool, not vendored); a swappable example_agent.py also exists in the official repo. See external_wrappers/repoprobe_reference_scaffold.py for the designed (not yet run) wrapper.
